response.sql:
WITH rated AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS films
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(films) AS avg_films FROM rated
),
above AS (
  SELECT r.films
  FROM rated r
  JOIN overall o ON r.films > o.avg_films
)
SELECT AVG(a.films) AS avg_count_above_average,
       AVG(a.films - o.avg_films) AS avg_excess_over_overall_average
FROM above a
CROSS JOIN overall o;

assumptions.assumption: Each rating counts once in the overall average (an unweighted mean of the per-rating distinct-film counts), and only ratings with at least one rented film appear in that mean. All five ratings in the verified data have rentals, so no rating is dropped.

A film counts as rented when at least one rental row links to one of its inventory copies. The inner joins drop rentals with no matching inventory or film, which is expected under the schema's foreign keys.

The 'average amount by which their count exceeds the overall average' is the mean of (rating count minus overall average) across the qualifying ratings. This equals the average qualifying count minus the overall average.
